title: The Iron Typewriter
premise: In the river city of Valdorra, on the eve of revolution, Coral Reyes has spent fifteen years hiding her father's forbidden craft — cutting typefaces for banned pamphlets — behind the respectable front of his print shop. When the seasonal bridge closes, trapping the city, a wounded courier arrives carrying a promise Coral made years ago to Elena Vasquez, now declared an enemy of the state: safe passage for Elena's daughter, hidden in plain sight among the print shop apprentices. As soldiers tighten their grip and informers circle closer, Coral must choose between the silences that kept her family alive and the justice her father's type once promised. In the end, she forges documents in her father's stolen typeface to smuggle the girl out on the last ferry before ice seals the river — sacrificing the shop, her father's freedom, and the quiet identity she built, but inheriting at last the true legacy of the iron typewriter.
about_author: Sable Marchetti is the pen name of a former letterpress restorer who spent a decade cataloguing underground printing presses in Eastern European archives. She writes historical fiction about the people history forgets — the hands that set the type while others made the speeches.

chapters.title: The Weight of Silence
chapters.summary: Coral Reyes works the family print shop in Valdorra, setting type by day and hiding her father Tomás's illegal typeface cuts beneath the floorboards by night. POV: Coral. The chapter establishes her careful choreography of silence and ends with news that the bridge will close within the week — the last road out of the city until spring.

chapters.title: A Promise Made in Peacetime
chapters.summary: Through flashback woven into present-day preparations, we learn of Coral's childhood friendship with Elena Vasquez and the vow exchanged at the riverside fifteen years ago: if either ever needed shelter, the other would give it without question. POV: Coral. The beat is bittersweet nostalgia shadowed by dread, as Elena's name appears on new government posters declaring her an enemy of the state.

chapters.title: The Courier at the Door
chapters.summary: On the night before the bridge closes, a wounded young courier collapses against the shop door carrying Elena's sealed letter and a hidden child, Lucia. POV: Coral, with a brief interlude from the courier's delirium. Coral must decide within hours whether to honor the promise; the emotional beat is terror transforming into fierce resolve as she takes them in.

chapters.title: Apprentice Number Four
chapters.summary: Coral fabricates papers making Lucia an apprentice, coaching the silent girl in ink-stained hands and printer's patter. Meanwhile Captain Ibarra of the garrison begins routine inspections of all shops. POV alternates between Coral and Lucia, whose guarded interiority reveals what she fled. The beat is claustrophobic tension laced with unexpected tenderness between the two girls.

chapters.title: What the Type Remembers
chapters.summary: Tomás discovers the truth and nearly turns Lucia out, forcing Coral to confront the rift between her father's survival philosophy and her own conscience. He reveals why he stopped cutting seditious type: a former apprentice was executed. POV: Coral with Tomás's confession at center. The beat is grief and generational fracture — inheritance questioned rather than received.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: A neighboring merchant, Señor Brill, who has long coveted the shop's riverfront lease, notices extra rations purchased and begins asking questions. Revolution ignites in the streets outside; curfews fall. POV: Coral, with one chilling scene from Brill's calculating perspective. The beat is paranoia tightening like a screw as the city itself becomes hostile territory.

chapters.title: Inspection
chapters.summary: Captain Ibarra searches the print shop during working hours while Lucia hides inside the press frame, ink dripping onto her sleeve. Coral performs the performance of her life, even pulling a proof sheet of loyalist broadsides to satisfy him. POV: Coral. The beat is white-knuckle suspense ending in hollow relief — and the knowledge that Brill saw everything through the window.

chapters.title: The Iron Typewriter
chapters.summary: Tomás, changed by the inspection, unlocks the floorboards and shows Coral the full archive: fifteen years of cut typefaces bearing names of the disappeared. He agrees to forge passage documents — the 'iron typewriter' of the title, the press as weapon. POV: Coral and Tomás in alternating scenes of reconciliation. The beat is hard-won unity and purpose, love expressed through craft.

chapters.title: Ice on the River
chapters.summary: Brill denounces the shop; soldiers come at dawn, but Coral has already sent Lucia to the docks with forged papers naming her a printer's daughter bound for her aunt across the river. Tomás stays behind to work the press as decoy and is arrested. POV: split between Coral at the dock watching the ferry slip away and Tomás in custody. The climax lands with the ice floes closing the channel minutes after the ferry crosses.

chapters.title: Setting the Next Line
chapters.summary: Weeks into winter, Coral visits her father in prison, bringing him proof sheets printed on his own type under her new imprint, 'Reyes & Daughter.' She has inherited not just the shop's ruins but its true purpose. POV: Coral, closing with her hand on the press lever. The beat is resolve born of loss — justice continued outside the law, one line of type at a time.
